en: Abhayākaragupta’s *Varṣāpaṇavidhi* After meditating on emptiness (*śūnyatā*), upon a multicolored lotus and a sun disk, a *Hūṃ* transforms into Vajragaruḍa—fierce, sixteen years of age, winged, with a black body and four faces (the first [front] dark; the left smoky; the right white; the upper is a garuḍa-head, red). He has eight arms: (right 1: vajra; left 1: noose and *tarjanī*; right 2: skin; left 2: skull-cup; right 3: skull-staff; left 3: elephant goad; right 4: ...).

[He holds] a *ḍamaru*, has matted hair topped with a crossed-vajra (*viśvavajra*) and a crescent moon, wears the six bone ornaments and a tiger skin, and stands in the *ālīḍha* posture upon the white Varuṇa and the tail of a *nāga*.

His retinue consists of: in the east, white Ananta; in the north, dark blue Vāsuki; in the west, red Takṣaka; in the south, green Padma; in the northeast, white Mahāpadma; in the northwest, smoke-colored Śaṅkhapāla; in the southeast, grey Karkoṭa; and in the southwest, yellow Anantatapta. All are three-headed, with palms joined in prayer, awaiting the Lord’s command, and filled with awe.

Facing east before a cloth painting (*paṭa*) of the Lord, he should visualize the mantra *hūṃ naṃ hūṃ* at the hearts of the nine attendants. Then, he should perform the preliminary service (*puraścaraṇa*) for that mantra (one hundred thousand recitations).

Having perfected the mantra, he should meditate fiercely and with composure, remaining silent and celibate. Then, at each junction (*saṃdhyā*), he should offer oblations of milk and other substances into the fire while reciting ten thousand times the prescribed mantras of the attendants. He should visualize Garuḍa... [them]. Another mantra is to be recited. After seven days, it will rain.

Another procedure, which is smokeless [i.e., without a *homa*-fire], is taught for the purpose of stopping excessive rain. The mantras are provided. At the conclusion [of both procedures], a *pūjā* is performed and the *śatākṣara* mantra is recited [to compensate for any deficiencies].
NB: The lineage is given as Vanaratna, Sarvamitra, Ravicandra, and Rūparāja, the scribe.
Palm-leaf Tokyo composite manuscript, beginning at folio 25r1 [catalogue no. 936]; no title given, new number 307 V, old number 306; dated saṃvat 589, Hook-topped Newari script.
Paper Tokyo composite manuscript, beginning at folio 209v5 [catalogue no. 1016]; titled “Collection of 26-”, old number 293; dated saṃvat 901, Common Newari script. oṃ namaḥ śrīvajrasattvāya ||
Oṃ, homage to the glorious Vaśattva!
Immediately after emptiness, having instantly visualized an eight-petaled lotus with petals colored according to their respective directions;

immediately after emptiness, instantly [visualizing] an eight-petaled lotus with petals colored according to their respective directions. In its pericarp, upon a sun disk, is the syllable *hūṃ-jaṃ*, the venerable lord named Vajragaruḍa.

In its pericarp, upon a sun disk, one should visualize the Bhagavān named Vajragaruḍa, born from the syllable *hūṃ*; he is black in color, terrifying with protruding eyes, four-faced, eight-armed, wrathful, and sixteen years of age.
One should visualize him as black in color, terrifying with protruding eyes, four-faced, eight-armed, wrathful, and sixteen years of age.

His first [face] is blue, the right is grey, the left is dark green, and the upper one has the face of a garuḍa; his first [face] is blue, the right is smoky-grey, the left is dark green, and the upper one has the face of a garuḍa;
he is red, with fierce rays like twelve suns, three eyes on each face, and endowed with two wings.

Red in color, like twelve suns, with a fierce egg-like face, three eyes on each countenance, and endowed with two wings; with his right hand brandishing a vajra, and his left hand holding a noose and a threatening gesture (*tarjanī*).
With his right hand brandishing a vajra, and his left hand holding a noose and a threatening gesture.

Furthermore, with the other left and right hands, he likewise holds a shield and a garment in due order, and he holds a skull-cup and a khaṭvāṅga staff. Likewise, he holds a goad and a ḍamaru drum. He wears a crown of matted hair adorned with a double-vajra and a crescent moon; his crown is endowed with the six seals (mudrās) and he wears a garland of severed heads.

Thus, having visualized [the deity] wearing a crown adorned with a *viśvavajra* beneath a *jaṭāmakuṭa*, holding a hook (*aṅkuśa*) and a *bhramarūka* [in his hands], endowed with the six seals (*ṣaṇmudrā*), wearing a garland of severed heads, and clad in a tiger skin; pressing his lower lip with his fangs; and treading upon the white Varuṇa, whose tail is that of another nāga, with his legs in the *ālīḍha* posture. Having visualized him as wearing a tiger skin, pressing his lower lip with his fangs, and treading upon the white Varuṇa, whose tail is that of another nāga, with his legs in the *ālīḍha* posture.
On the eastern, northern, western, and southern petals, one should visualize Ananta, Vāsuki, Takṣaka, and Padma, respectively, as white, blue, red, and green.
On the eastern, northern, western, and southern petals, one should visualize Ānanda, Vāsuki, Takṣaka, and Padma, respectively, as white, blue, red, and green.
In the northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest corners, one should visualize Mahāpadma, Śaṅkhapāla, Karkoṭaka, and Ananta, as yellow, smoky-grey, ash-grey, green, and yellow, respectively.

In the intermediate directions of the northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest, one should visualize Mahāpadma, Śaṅkhapāla, Karkoṭaka, Ānanda, Taptaka, Pīta, Dhūmra, Dhūsara, and Harita— both [groups of] nāgas with three red hoods,
their palms joined in reverence, gazing at the Blessed One. All the nāgas have three red hoods and, with palms joined in reverence, gaze at the Blessed One.
Seeking his command, they are fearful and should be meditated upon;
those seeking his command, being fearful, should be meditated upon.
In that regard, having meditated on *hūṃ naṃ hūṃ* in the heart of each of the nine [deities] beginning with Varuṇa,
There, having visualized "HŪṂ NAṂ HŪṂ" in the heart of each of the nine [deities] beginning with Varuṇa,
the mantra-practitioner, facing eastward, stands before the cloth painting of Vajragaruḍa.
Facing east, the mantra-practitioner stands before the painting of Vajragaruḍa and recites:
*oṃ vajranārāyaṇa nipaya vahnim navāmbumeghaiḥ hūṃ hūṃ*.
Oṃ vajramīnārāyaṇa, extinguish the offering with floods of water! Hūṃ hūṃ!
One should recite this mantra one hundred thousand times.
One should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times;
therein this mantra becomes accomplished.
In this regard, this mantra becomes accomplished.

Once it is accomplished, one who is devoted to the meditation on the Great Wrathful One, remaining silent and observing celibacy, eating milk-rice and offering meals of sweet milk at each junction of the day (saṃdhyā), performing oblations with fuel from milk-trees and milk for Varuṇa and for the individual nāgas, should recite the mantra ten million times (ayuta).

When success had been achieved, he, endowed with the meditation on the Great Wrathful One, remained celibate and subsisted on milk-rice; providing milk-drinks and milk-meals to those who ate milk-rice, he performed oblations at each junction of the day using milk-tree fuel and milk. Having offered to Varuṇa and to the Nāgas, he recited ten thousand repetitions (*ayuta*) of each of their mantras: *Oṃ aṃ Anantāya hūṃ naṃ hūṃ varṣaya svāhā*.
Oṃ aṃ to bliss hūṃ naṃ hūṃ cause it to rain svāhā!
Oṃ vāṃ to Vāsuki, hūṃ naṃ hūṃ, cause it to rain! Svāhā!
Oṃ vāṃ to Vāsuki, hūṃ naṃ hūṃ, cause it to rain, svāhā!
Oṃ taṃ to Takṣaka, hūṃ naṃ hūṃ, cause rain to fall! Svāhā!
Oṃ taṃ to Takṣaka, hūṃ naṃ hūṃ, cause it to rain, svāhā!
Oṃ paṃ to the lotus, hūṃ naṃ hūṃ, cause it to rain, svāhā!
Oṃ paṃ, to the lotus, hūṃ naṃ hūṃ, cause it to rain, svāhā!
Oṃ śaṃ śaṃkhapālāya hūṃ naṃ hūṃ, cause rain to fall! Svāhā!
Oṃ śaṃ śaṃkhapālāya hūṃ naṃ hūṃ, cause rain to fall, svāhā!
Oṃ kaṃ karkoṭāya hūṃ naṃ hūṃ varṣaya svāhā!
Oṃ kaṃ karkoṭāya hūṃ naṃ hūṃ rain down, svāhā!
Oṃ aṃ, to the one who is eternally heated, hūṃ naṃ hūṃ, cause it to rain, svāhā!
Oṃ aṃ to Anavatapta, hūṃ naṃ hūṃ, cause it to rain, svāhā!
Oṃ vaṃ, to Varuṇa, the lord of the nāgas, cause the nāgas to rain; hūṃ naṃ hūṃ svāhā!
Oṃ vaṃ! To Varuṇa, the lord of the nāgas, cause the nāgas to rain; hūṃ naṃ hūṃ svāhā!
Thereafter, one should meditate that Vajragaruḍa extinguishes the limitless fires with the wind from his wings and dries up the rivers with the light from his beak.
Thereafter, the Vajra-Garuḍa, with his sword-like beak, extinguishes the fire of the Yakṣas and the winds by means of the light from his beak; one should visualize him as making the rivers flow.
One should recite the mantra: *Oṃ vajranārāyaṇa nirvāpaya vahniṃ navāmbumeghaiḥ hūṃ hūṃ*. One should mutter the mantra.
Oṃ vajranārāyaṇa, extinguish the fire; do not [let it be] by clouds of water! Hūṃ hūṃ. One should recite this mantra.
Then, within seven nights, all the nāgas cause a downpour of water.
Then, after seven nights have passed, all the nāgas cause a downpour of water.

One who is well-prepared should offer smokeless guggulu and sarjarasa resin into the mouths of elephants that have been clothed in garments; by reciting the mantra while throwing it into their mouths, one wards off excessive rain.

One should offer *atiṣṭhāguggulu*, resin of the *sarja* tree, and *nirdhūma-nāgānāṃ-patāva-stitā* into a fire while reciting [the mantra]; by casting these into the rain, one who is chanting wards off excessive rain.
One should perform the meditation as before;
one should perform the meditation as before.
Oṃ ā vajravaruṇāya hūṃ svāhā.
Oṃ āḥ vajravaruṇāya hūṃ svāhā.
Oṃ āḥ to Ananta hūṃ svāhā.
Oṃ āḥ to bliss hūṃ svāhā.

In this manner, having uttered each of their respective mantras and worshipped with white flowers, and while making the gesture of the hood with the left hand, having again uttered each of their respective mantras and worshipped with white flowers, [one should perform] the gesture of the hood with the left hand.

Reciting the *nāgabali* mantra: "Oṃ bhakṣa 2 āgaccha 2 mahānāgādhipati sarvabhūrbhūvaḥ phū phū svāhā," one should consecrate the milk offering (*kṣīrabali*). Reciting the *nāgabali* mantra: "Oṃ bhakṣa 2 āgaccha 2 mahānāgādhipati sarvabhūbhūvaḥ pha pha svāhā," one should consecrate the milk offering.
One should perform worship as before, recite the *satākṣara* [mantra], and ask for forgiveness.
One should perform worship as before, recite the hundred-syllable mantra, and ask for forgiveness.
The ritual for the commencement of the rains retreat is completed.
The procedure for the Varṣāpaṇa is completed.
The work of the great scholar, the venerable Śrī Abhayākaragupta.

The work of the great paṇḍita, the venerable Abhayākaragupta. [211v3] Transcribed by Rūparāja, the disciple in the lineage of the venerable Vanaratnapāda and the venerable Sarvamitra, and [the disciple of] Ravicandra.
